name: RBI-prescribed savings deposit rate (all banks, until deregulation on 25 Oct 2011)
notes: Points are [effectiveFrom, rate, note]; rate is null where RBI set two rates (the note explains).

No rate levels located for the savings deposit rate before July 1, 1977. The RBI Handbook 'Structure of Interest Rates' tables examined in this pass (Table 39 of the Handbook of Monetary Statistics of India, and successor Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy editions) carry a 'Savings' column only from FY2003-04 onward in the editions retrieved; earlier editions of that same table (1970-71 onward) in this pass did not include a savings-deposit column at all -- only term-deposit buckets. The 1977-2003 rate levels above come from a secondary source (IIT Bombay technical report) that itself cites RBI Credit Policy statements; treat as needing primary-source (RBI Annual Report / Credit Policy statement text) verification before publishing, per Standard #2.
Two small (1-day) date discrepancies between sources are flagged in the 'note' fields above (March 1 vs 2, 1978; March 1 vs 2, 2003) and NOT resolved -- do not silently pick one.

The exact date NRE/NRO savings deposits (as opposed to resident domestic savings deposits) were deregulated is inconsistently reported across RBI's own circulars for different bank categories (commercial banks: Dec 16 and Dec 28, 2011 respectively for NRE and NRO; Urban Co-op Bank Master Circular Annex: Nov 25 and Dec 28, 2011). Flagged in the last row's note.
points: Savings-with-cheque-facility 3.0%; savings-without-cheque-facility 5.0% (RBI Credit Policy of May 27, 1977, split the single savings account into two categories effective July 1, 1977)
Declared 4.5% p.a.; effective yield ~3.8% p.a. per IIT-Bombay technical note (due to pre-2010 interest-calculation method: minimum balance between 10th and last day of month)
Declared 6.0% p.a. (the highest level the RBI-prescribed savings rate ever reached); effective yield ~5.1% p.a.
Declared 4.5% p.a.; effective yield ~3.8% p.a. (IIT-Bombay note states this level held 'November 1, 1994 through March 31, 2000')
Declared 3.5% p.a.; effective yield ~3.0% p.a. until the interest-calculation method changed on 2010-04-01 (see next row)

Rate unchanged at 3.5% p.a., but interest now calculated on a DAILY PRODUCT basis (RBI circular, effective April 1, 2010) instead of the old 10th-to-month-end minimum-balance method, so the effective yield rose to the full declared 3.5%
Declared and effective 4.0% p.a. (daily-product method already in force)

DEREGULATED for resident-Indian domestic savings deposits: banks free to set their own rate, subject to (i) uniform rate up to Rs 1 lakh balance and (ii) optional differential rate(s) above Rs 1 lakh, with no discrimination between similar deposits accepted the same day.
